bugLocation: src/cache_sweep.py — evict_expired(): `entries.pop(index)` followed by an unconditional `index += 1`
bugSummary: The sweep pops from the list it is walking by index and always advances the index, so the entry that shifts into a just-vacated slot is skipped; two adjacent expired entries leave the second one live.
minimalFix: Build the survivors as a new list instead of mutating under the index: `return [entry for entry in entries if entry["expires_at"] > now]` (or only advance the index in the else branch).
survivalStory: evict_expired reads correctly in isolation and for every namespace whose expired entries are separated by live ones or sit last; it only over-counts the rare namespace with two adjacent expired entries, which the happy-path fixtures (isolated expirations) never exercised, and the inflated count still looks like a plausible per-namespace number.

redHerrings.looksWrongBecause: the `<=` invites a `<`-vs-`<=` off-by-one suspicion on the expiry boundary
redHerrings.provablyInnocentBecause: the data contract declares an entry whose expires_at equals now to be expired, and catalog's c-1 sits exactly at now, so `<=` is correct; changing it to `<` would break the currently-correct catalog row and has no effect on sessions, so it cannot cause the inflation

redHerrings.looksWrongBecause: trimming fields looks like it could merge or split namespaces and drop data
redHerrings.provablyInnocentBecause: the contract declares surrounding whitespace trimmed, so ` feed ` and feed are one namespace by design; the strip is load-bearing (it folds feed's f-2 into the feed bucket) and removing it would split feed into two rows, the opposite of the observed single-row inflation

complexityAnswer.dominantCost: a single linear pass to parse and bucket the n log rows, then a linear sweep per namespace; the only sort is over the handful of namespaces for output ordering (O(k log k), k namespaces)

debriefRubric: Reproduced with the run command and diffed against the oracle before opening the source.
Localized the inflated value to the sessions row and named the skipped-after-pop entry (s-2 stepped over when s-1 was removed) as the cause, in one sentence.
Shipped a minimal fix (iterate a snapshot / build a new list, or guard the index advance) rather than rewriting the sweep.
Tested the `<=` expiry boundary against the contract (catalog's c-1 at exactly now) and cleared it instead of chasing it.
Tested the field strip normalization against the contract and cleared it instead of chasing it.
Complexity: identified the linear parse and per-namespace sweep as O(n) and noted the only sort is over the namespaces.
Phase-2: adapted evict_expired to exempt pinned entries, recognizing the pinned flag was already parsed and thrown away, instead of rewriting.
Recommend exactly one drill: for a weak sweep pass, a mutation-during-iteration drill; for a weak phase-2, an adapt-vs-rewrite drill.
